title: The Cave Story and Saying 'If Allah Wills'

paragraphs.text: Allah made the hearts of the youths firm. They said their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth, and they would never call on any other deity. No one is more unjust than one who lies about Allah. So they left their people and went to the cave, hoping for Allah's mercy.

The sun turned away from their cave when it rose and when it set. A person would think them awake, but they were asleep. Allah turned them right and left, while their dog stretched its legs at the entrance. When Allah woke them, they thought they had stayed a day or part of a day. They sent one of them to the city with a silver coin to buy food. He had to be careful, because people might stone them.

Allah let people find them, so they would know His promise is true. People argued about them and decided to build a masjid over them. Some guessed their number, but only Allah and a few know. Never say you will do something tomorrow without adding, "If Allah wills." They stayed in the cave three hundred and nine years.

Recite the Book of your Lord; no one can change His words. Stay patient with those who call on their Lord morning and evening. Do not obey one whose heart is careless and who follows his desire. A fire waits for the wrongdoers, but the reward of those who do good will never be lost.

hardWords.m: the place where you go in
